Ransomware recovery · mid-sized manufacturer

The difference between having backups and having a recovery plan.

This fictional walkthrough shows how preparation changes the first eight hours of a disruptive cyber incident.

Fictional operational scenario
180Employees across two facilities
4 hoursRequired recovery target for order processing
30 minAcceptable data-loss window
3 prioritiesIdentity, production scheduling and customer communications

A rehearsed sequence reduces improvisation.

07:42

Detection creates a decision, not another alert

Abnormal encryption behavior is confirmed. The pre-agreed incident lead activates containment authority.

08:05

Identity and affected segments are contained

Compromised sessions are revoked while the production boundary remains isolated from corporate services.

09:10

Recovery order follows business impact

Order processing and production scheduling take priority over lower-impact internal systems.

10:25

Clean recovery begins from a verified point

Immutable copies and tested procedures remove guesswork about data integrity and restoration steps.

12:06

Critical workflow returns under monitoring

Operations resume in a controlled state while investigation and broader restoration continue.

What changed the outcome

The controls were connected before the pressure arrived.

01

Named authority

Containment did not wait for an improvised approval chain.

02

Business recovery order

Technical teams already knew which workflow came back first.

03

Proven recovery point

Restore decisions relied on evidence, not hope.
